extracted.intended_audience: aircraft operators, maintenance personnel, continuing airworthiness managers, FAA certification/maintenance inspectors, and interested public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Reading and implementing FAA proposed airworthiness directives (NPRMs) for specific airplane models, including required inspections/modifications, compliance times, alternate means procedures, special flight-permit authority, and public-comment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance time (Boeing 737-400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance required within the next 1,000 hours time-in-service after the effective date of this AD, unless previously accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the mandatory compliance window for the required action to prevent APU rotor failure; operators must track TIS and ensure action before the 1,000-hour threshold unless already done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required modification — APU EGT indication (Boeing 737-400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the APU instrumentation wiring in a manner that will assure continuous flight-compartment APU exhaust gas temperature (EGT) indication following an APU shutdown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The modification must be accomplished in a manner approved by the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region. The FAA may reference a manufacturer service bulletin as an approved method of compliance if the bulletin is approved prior to issuance of the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate means of compliance (AMOC) routing (Boeing 737-400 and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an acceptable level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office (or Manager, Standardization Branch, ANM-113 as specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI), who will either concur or comment, and then send it to the appropriate Manager for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special flight permits authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Special flight permits may be issued in accordance with FAR 21.197 and 21.199 to operate airplanes to a base in order to comply with the requirements of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits allow ferrying an aircraft to a location where AD-required work can be accomplished; operators should follow FAR 21.197/21.199 procedures when requesting such permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service information availability and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons affected by this directive may obtain copies of related service information by contacting the manufacturer; these documents may be examined at specified FAA offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM includes manufacturer contact details (e.g., Boeing Commercial Airplanes address, British Aerospace librarian) and FAA regional office locations where service bulletins can be reviewed. Operators should obtain and follow the referenced service bulletin procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost impact estimation (informational)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated number of affected U.S. airplanes, manhours per airplane, average labor cost per manhour, parts cost estimate, and total cost impact on U.S. operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM provides these figures (e.g., 18 airplanes, 10 manhours, $40/hr => $7,200) as the agency's economic impact estimate; operators may use or rebut these estimates in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetitive inspection requirement (BAC 1-11 200/400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform repetitive dye penetrant or eddy current inspections to detect cracks in the retraction jack attachment arm lugs on the nose landing gear housing, in accordance with British Aerospace Alert Service Bulletin 32-A-PM5946, Issue 1, dated April 6, 1987.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inspection method, scope, and procedures are defined by the referenced service bulletin; classification by the UK CAA as mandatory is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection compliance interval and scope (BAC 1-11 200/400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the accumulation of 15,000 landings or within 150 landings after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 15,000 landings, perform a dye penetrant or eddy current inspection of the lower faces of both lugs over an area not less than 0.5 inch forward and aft of change in lug section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies initial and repetitive inspection timing measured in landings and the minimum inspected area; operators must track landings and ensure inspections meet the dimensional scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action if cracks found (BAC 1-11 200/400)
rubrics_metrics.description: If cracks are found, repair or replace with a serviceable part, prior to further flight, in accordance with the referenced service bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repairs or replacements must follow the service bulletin instructions and be completed before the airplane is dispatched for further flight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability by modification status (BAe-146 HCM50075 mods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to Model BAe-146 series airplanes on which modifications HCM50075A, B, and C have been incorporated, certificated in any category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must determine applicability based on their airplanes' incorporated modifications; AD compliance applies only to affected airplanes as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance time — 30 days (BAe-146 entries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance is required within 30 days after the effective date of this AD, unless previously accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short fixed calendar-time compliance window; operators must schedule and complete the required action within 30 days or show prior accomplishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect and secure quick-disconnect couplings (BAe-146 HCM50075 mods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspect the quick-disconnect couplings in the yellow and auxiliary systems hydraulic lines to the wheel brake units for being finger tight, retighten to finger-tight torque and secure the quick-disconnect couplings with a corrosion-resistant steel lockwire, in accordance with British Aerospace Service Bulletin 32-A101, dated September 1, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the inspection (finger tight check), required retorque ('finger-tight torque'), and locking method (corrosion-resistant steel lockwire); follow the referenced service bulletin for procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placard installation requirement (BAe 146-100A/-200A/-300A and BAe 148 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Install a warning placard on shelf No. 5 beneath the flap computer stating 'WARNING: THIS EQUIPMENT MUST NOT BE REMOVED OR RE-RACKED IN FLIGHT' and install a warning placard on circuit breaker panel 131-11-00 stating 'WARNING—C/BREAKERS MUST NOT BE PULLED IN FLIGHT', in accordance with British Aerospace Service Bulletin 11-36-01104A&B, dated May 10, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exact placard location and wording; operators must install placards per the service bulletin to prevent in-flight removal/re-racking of equipment or pulling breakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability by serial number (BAe 148 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to Model BAe 148-100A, Serial Numbers E1002 through E1100, E1102, and E1103; Model BAe 148-200A, Serial Numbers E2012 through E2113, E2115 and E2118; and Model BAe 148-300A, Serial Numbers E3118 through E3123 and E3125; certificated in any category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must check serial-number applicability lists to determine whether the AD applies to a particular airframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of UK CAA/manufacturer service bulletin as compliance method
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM references specific manufacturer/CAA service bulletins (classified by UK CAA as mandatory) as the procedures to be followed for inspections, repairs, modifications, and placard installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service bulletin is the procedural norm; FAA may accept the bulletin procedures as the approved method of compliance or reference them in the final rule if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission procedures (FAA NPRMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Send comments on the proposal in duplicate to the Federal Aviation Administration at the specified regional Transport Airplane Directorate address and identify the regulatory docket number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be submitted by the stated deadline (dates provided in each NPRM). All communications received on or before the closing date will be considered by the Administrator before taking action on the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of comments requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are specifically invited on the overall regulatory, economic, environmental, and energy aspects of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should address these aspects if relevant; the agency may change proposals in light of comments received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of comments and docket materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments submitted will be available, both before and after the closing date for comments, in the Rules Docket for examination by interested persons. A report summarizing each FAA/public contact concerned with the substance of the proposal will be filed in the Rules Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested persons may examine docketed comments and supporting materials at the specified Rules Docket locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of comment receipt (postcard request)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters wishing the FAA to acknowledge receipt of their comments must submit a self-addressed, stamped postcard stating 'Comments to Docket Number [X]'; the post card will be date/time stamped and returned to the commenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an optional administrative convenience for commenters who want formal receipt acknowledgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory certifications & draft evaluation availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency certifies whether the proposed regulation is (1) not a 'major rule' under Executive Order 12291; (2) not a 'significant rule' under DOT Regulatory Policies and Procedures; and (3) will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the Regulatory Flexibility Act. A copy of the draft evaluation prepared for this action is contained in the regulatory docket and may be obtained from the Rules Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These certifications explain the agency's compliance with executive orders and statutes; commenters may review and comment on the draft evaluation in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing procedures (IRS notice example)
rubrics_metrics.description: For public hearings on proposed regulations, outlines of oral comments must be mailed by the specified date; requests to speak and outlines should be submitted to the stated address. Each speaker will be limited to 10 minutes for oral presentation exclusive of panel questions and answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of controlled access, attendees may be restricted until a stated time; an agenda will be made after outlines are received and copies will be available at the hearing.
